data.name: CarIntro
data.value: Everything after the form is what the controller is running with, resolved from the configuration at startup. The form changes what the next start reads; a restart applies it, and then the account below is where it gets proved.

data.name: PortalIntro
data.value: Asks {0} for {1}, once, when you press the button. {2} runs on no schedule and what it shows is fed to nothing — not the dashboard's card, not any charging decision — so it is how you check that the credentials work and that the portal's fields are understood, whether or not the feed on its own clock is switched on.

data.name: PortalFieldsHint
data.value: Those are the {0}, {1}, {2} and {3} fields in the form above; fill them in and restart. The portal also needs a {4} enabling by hand before it delivers anything — see {5}.

data.name: SignsInAfresh
data.value: Each press signs in afresh. That is fine by hand and is why this is not a poll: repeatedly replaying a password at a real identity provider is how accounts get locked.

data.name: FeedIntro
data.value: Asks {0} for {1}, once, now — the same call the feed makes on its own clock, made because you asked rather than because the clock said so. Unlike a Data Act read, what comes back {2} reach the dashboard's card: an owner who presses a button is asking the whole UI to catch up, not just this page. It does not disturb the feed's own cadence.

data.name: FeedAskHint
data.value: If the account above is not signed in, this is what says so: the feed answers with what is stopping it rather than with a reading.

data.name: NothingToAskYet
data.value: Nothing to ask yet: this feed is switched on but did not start, so the controller has no client for it. Fill in the fields it needs in the form above and restart.

data.name: NothingToAskChargeOnly
data.value: Nothing to ask, because nothing reads this car — and nothing here needs to. Whether a cable is in the socket comes from the charger rather than from the car, so the dashboard answers that either way; what no feed costs is the pack's own state of charge, and a target is asked for in kWh instead.

data.name: WorthRetrying
data.value: Worth pressing again — this one is expected and usually clears itself.

data.name: NotWorthRetrying
data.value: Pressing again will not help. This one needs something changed, or a browser.

data.name: NothingOnTheCard
data.value: Nothing has reached the dashboard's card yet, so there is nothing to hold this against. That is what an install with no feed switched on looks like, and it is not a fault: this press is the whole reading.

data.name: FreshFrom
data.value: Fresh, from {0}, and the dashboard's card is now showing it too.

data.name: AlreadyHeld
data.value: That is the reading the feed was already holding, not a new one.

data.name: NothingDescribed
data.value: Nothing is described yet, so every charging limit is the installation's own and no target can be asked for as a state of charge. That is a supported installation — the charge still runs — and the form above is how to change it.

data.name: NarrowerOfTwo
data.value: The controller works to the narrower of the two. A car can only ever {0} a limit — the installation's maximum is the site's supply and the wiring in the wall, not a preference — and anything the car leaves unstated is simply the installation's figure.

data.name: NoManufacturerFeed
data.value: No manufacturer feed is running. Charging is unaffected; what is missing is the car's own state of charge, so a target is asked for in kWh rather than as a percentage.

data.name: CarBatteryPressHint
data.value: The car's own state of charge, as the source answered this press. Not the home battery.

data.name: CarRangeHint
data.value: What the car reckons is left in it, off its own recent consumption. Nothing here plans on it; it is the figure that says whether the charge you are about to ask for is enough.

data.name: CarReadingAgeHint
data.value: How long ago the car itself produced this reading — not how long ago you pressed the button. Hours old is normal for a parked car.

data.name: CarChargeStateHint
data.value: What the car says it is doing: Idle, Charging, Complete, or Unknown when it doesn't report.

data.name: CarPlugStateHint
data.value: Whether the car says a cable is in its socket. A separate reading from the charger's own status, and a much slower one.

data.name: TargetSocHint
data.value: The car's own charge limit, set in the car or its app. The Data Act portal carries it and no live feed does: no plan reads it yet (#101). A dash means this source did not carry it.

data.name: TimeLeftHint
data.value: The car's own estimate of how much longer it needs, not one of ours. A dash means the source did not carry it — which is itself a finding.

data.name: CaptureTimeNote
data.value: The capture time is the {0}, not this moment's. A parked car reporting hours ago is normal and not a fault — its state of charge does not drift.

data.name: OwnTopicNothingToPress
data.value: Nothing to press, because nothing here fetches: you publish this car's readings yourself on {0} — one JSON object per reading, with the {1} own capture time in {2} and {3}, {4}, {5} and {6} as far as your source carries them.
data.comment: {0} is the topic (or TheTopicInTheForm), {1} is OwnTopicNothingToPress_Cars in italics, {2}–{6} are JSON field names.

data.name: TheTopicInTheForm
data.value: the topic in the form above

data.name: LastArrived
data.value: The last one arrived carrying {0}, captured {1} ago.

data.name: NothingArrived
data.value: Nothing has arrived on it yet.

data.name: CardShowing
data.value: The dashboard's card is showing {0} from {1}, captured {2} ago{3}. That is a different session asking at a different moment, so a difference is not by itself a fault.
data.comment: {3} is SameSoc or PointsBelow/PointsAbove, with its leading space, or nothing.

data.name: OwnTopicToo
data.value: This car also has a topic of its own, {0}. It may run beside a manufacturer feed — the freshest reading wins.

data.name: CarReadOnly
data.value: Read-only, because this UI has no login. These fields include a manufacturer account's password, and without a login anyone on the LAN could read the car or change which account it is read from. Configure {0} ({1}) and they become editable here; until then, change them in {2} and restart.

data.name: CarSaveNote
data.value: A save is checked the way startup checks the configuration, and writes only what differs to {0}. That file wins over {1} key by key, so each field says where its value comes from. Nothing changes until the controller restarts — and a save cannot prove an account, because the feed is built at startup from these keys. Restart, then {2} and ask the car.

data.name: SignInIdChanged
data.value: The brand's sign-in id has changed

data.name: SignInIdChangedNote
data.value: The portal's client ids are reverse-engineered rather than published, so one can go stale without warning — the symptom is a sign-in that fails as though the password were wrong. Stating an id here overrides the brand above.

data.name: CarFieldsNote
data.value: These are the fields that make charging correct, and they are independent of any feed. The installation allows {0}–{1} A; the controller works to the narrower of the two, and a car can only ever lower a limit.

data.name: NotSaved
data.value: Not saved — the controller would refuse to start with this:

data.name: HintUsablePack
data.value: usable, not the brochure's gross figure

data.name: HintMinCurrent
data.value: the lowest the car will start on

data.name: SavedRestartSignIn
data.value: Saved. Restart the controller to apply it, then sign in.

data.name: SavedRunning
data.value: Saved. The controller is already running with these values.

data.name: KeptInSecretStore
data.value: Kept in the secret store — {0}. Left empty it is unchanged; Remove clears it.

data.name: FeedDataAct
data.value: Audi · SEAT · Cupra · Bentley · VW commercial

data.name: FreshVolkswagen
data.value: about 20 s, plug state, live while charging

data.name: NoteVolkswagen
data.value: volkswagen.de, read live. The first sign-in always wants a one-time code e-mailed to this account, so it is done under Account below, after the restart.

data.name: NoteSkoda
data.value: The MyŠkoda Public API. It takes no password: create an API key in the MyŠkoda app and paste it under Account below. Keys expire, which is why they are renewed there rather than here.

data.name: NoteDataAct
data.value: The EU Data Act portal — the route for a Group brand with no live feed of its own. It delivers batches rather than readings, so expect the car's state of charge to be hours old, and no plug state at all.

data.name: NoteOwnTopic
data.value: An MQTT topic you publish to yourself. The broker and its credentials are the house broker's and stay in the Vehicle section; only the topic is the car's.

data.name: NoteNone
data.value: No feed, which is a supported installation and not an unfinished form: every EV with a Type 2 inlet charges without one. It costs exactly one thing — a target is asked for in kWh rather than as a state of charge, because nothing reports what the pack already holds.

data.name: TitleWebUi
data.value: Saved from this page in {0}; overrides .env.

data.name: TitleEnvironment
data.value: {0}, from .env under Docker or /etc/gleanvolt/gleanvolt.env under systemd.

data.name: TitleCommandLine
data.value: A command-line argument, which wins over this page.

data.name: TitleDefault
data.value: Set nowhere; the built-in default applies.

data.name: Empty
data.comment: A field the car reported with no value.

data.name: AccountDataAct
data.value: This portal signs in on each read, so there is no session to establish here. The account is the VW ID and password in the form above, and asking the car below is what proves them.

data.name: AccountOwnTopic
data.value: Nothing here signs in: you publish the readings yourself, so there is no manufacturer account in between. The broker's own credentials are the house broker's and stay in the Vehicle section.

data.name: AccountChargeOnly
data.value: No account, because nothing reads this car. Charging is unaffected — a target is asked for in kWh rather than as a state of charge.

data.name: NoAccountYet
data.value: There is no account to sign in to yet.

data.name: DiagnosticsIntro_0
data.value: why is that field a dash

data.name: DiagnosticsIntro
data.value: What the portal delivered and how much of it this build understands. This is what answers {0} — worth opening when a figure above is missing, and worth ignoring when none is.

data.name: FieldMoments
data.value: Each with the moment the {0} reported it. A read merges several deliveries, so two figures here can be hours apart — and comparing them without that is how a coarse reading and a stale one get mistaken for each other.

data.name: NothingInVocabulary
data.value: Not one field in the bundle is in the vocabulary at all — so this is a set of names to add rather than a car reporting empty values.

data.name: NeverBecameReading
data.value: What the bundle held that never became a reading

data.name: UnmappedNote
data.value: If a value above is missing, its real name is probably in this list — the portal's vocabulary was written down from VW's data dictionary rather than from your car, so this is expected on a first run rather than a fault. Adding the right names to {0} is the fix; pasting this list into an issue is enough for somebody else to do it.

data.name: AllRecognised
data.value: Every field in the bundle was recognised.

data.name: OdometerNote
data.value: The odometer is carried but nothing reads it. Target SOC is the one that would let a plan refuse an impossible battery target, deferred on {0}.

data.name: PhasesNotStated
data.value: Not stated — the installation's count is used

data.name: NoAccountExplanation
data.value: No manufacturer account is wired up, so there is nothing to sign in to. A feed that needs one brings its own sign-in as soon as every field it requires is filled in and the controller has restarted into them.
